# Critic-lane contract hardening: override binding, sibling admission, severity disclosure

Collates #3358, #3337, #3341 (one PR, user-authorized collation).

## What changed

- **Override activation is structural, not prose** (#3358 AC1, #3337 AC1): the critic and reviewer agent prompts no longer carry a phrase-activated PR-review exception — a plan or spec quoting "CONTROLLER-BOUND PR WORKFLOW CONTRACT" can no longer suspend PLAN REVIEW or the Stage-B mandate on non-PR runs. The suspension is now a controller-authored clause injected only into bound `swarm-pr-review:critic` lane blocks (`CRITIC_PROTOCOL_SELECTION_CLAUSE`), beside the existing reviewer clause. Non-PR critic and reviewer runs carry no PR-review text at all.
- **PR critic lanes verify the effective prompt** (#3358 AC2): admission refuses a critic agent registered with a custom prompt — both `critic.md` (replacement) and `critic_append.md` (append) from the opencode-swarm prompts directory — because neither can be mechanically verified to keep the `[CRITIC]` row contract. A belt additionally asserts every composed critic lane prompt carries the suspension clause. **Policy awaiting owner confirmation**: this is a user-visible change; remediation is to remove the file and restart OpenCode (or run the review without PR critic lanes). Non-PR critic use is unaffected.
- **Earlier-semantics verdict rows are disclosed, never silently dropped** (#3358 AC3): a reviewer row rejected only by the v1→v2 CONFIRMED/NONE tightening (`PR_REVIEW_VERDICT_SEMANTICS_VERSION = 2`) is recorded on the composition (`semanticsMismatchedItemIds`) and, while still unclaimed, blocks N-of-M settlement with a dedicated disclosure naming the items — instead of surfacing as a generic missing-verdict failure.
- **Findings write contract enforces the transport rule** (#3358 AC4): a findings record with CONFIRMED + severity NONE is rejected at the write boundary; durable records read through a read-tolerant schema so pre-rule rows keep loading.
- **One reviewer composition per critic dispatch** (#3358 AC5): the critic preflight derives order-unstable ids and reviewer severities from one shared gate context (previously composed twice).
- **Idempotent contract application** (#3358 AC6): re-applying the PR workflow prompt contract to a lane already carrying its controller block succeeds with exactly one block; recognition is strip-and-rebuild, never authentication.
- **Reviewer severities render on their own lines** (#3358 AC7): `assigned_item_ids` keeps bare ids; each severity appears as `reviewer_severity: <id>=<SEV>`. A verbatim copy of the old decorated token (`c1 (HIGH)`) no longer voids the lane as an unassigned id.
- **Uniform sibling admission** (#3358 AC8): one exported `PR_REVIEW_PHASE_ADMITTED_ROLES` table governs dispatch admission (exact membership — a user-defined `council_*`-prefixed agent is no longer admitted to council lanes), the gate recorder, and artifact integrity (launch-time normalizedAgent).
- **Side-effect-free phase admission** (#3341): PR_REVIEW council/reviewer/critic lane admission (roles, launchability, critic prompt provenance, owned-lane refusal) runs before gate activation/binding, so a refused batch consumes no durable workflow state; the side-effect-free comment states this scope precisely.

## Feedback-round additions (2026-11-10)

- **Feedback verdict lanes keep their protocol suppression**: the phrase-activated overrides removed from the critic and reviewer agent prompts (#3358 AC1) had also been the only suppression the `swarm-pr-feedback` verdict lanes had. Mode-scoped `PROTOCOL SELECTION` clauses now cover `stage-b-reviewer` (`[STAGE-B-REVIEW]` rows), `closeout-reviewer` (`[CLOSEOUT-REVIEW]`), and `closeout-critic` (PLAN REVIEW suspension, `[CLOSEOUT-CRITIC]` rows). `stage-b-test` is unchanged (its agent never carried an override).
- **Critic row vocabulary: DOWNGRADED never carries NONE**: a critic dismissing a finding emi

# Fix: on OpenCode 2, a reply the host reports as cut off by the output limit or the content filter fails closed

## What

On OpenCode 2 the v2 adapter rebuilt each reply's v1 `info` from the model ids
only and dropped the assistant entry's `finish`. The shared provider-error
reader (`readProviderMessageError`) reports a reply the host ended early
(`finish: "length"` as `MessageOutputLengthError`, `finish: "content-filter"`
as `MessageContentFilterError`) only when it can see `finish`, so on OpenCode 2
such a reply read as a clean success. A reply truncated right after
`VERDICT: APPROVED` could therefore pass the full-auto oversight critic and the
other consumers of the shared reader there, while the same reply failed closed
on OpenCode 1 (since v7.192.4).

The adapter now copies the `finish` of the last assistant entry of the final
turn onto `info`, matching v1, where the reply's `info.finish` is the last
step's. When the host reports a `length` or `content-filter` finish on a reply
whose final turn has no failed idle marker, has text or an idle marker, and
has no recorded error, the consumers of the shared reader now treat it as a
failed dispatch on both hosts, except the Lean lane runner, which keeps its
existing exemption for it. In the
Epic phase review, a textless reply of that kind no longer reads as the empty
provider-refusal signal: it skips the bash retry and fails that role's
dispatch (a `REJECTED` verdict, `dispatch: failed`), as on OpenCode 1. The
error is classified as permanent, so no fallback model is tried either.

Not changed: when OpenCode 2 reports the cut-off as a failed step
(`session.execution.failed`, a recorded error), the adapter still takes its
recorded-error path, which fails closed under the recorded error's own name,
so the Lean runner's exemption does not apply there (unless that name is
itself `MessageOutputLengthError` or `MessageContentFilterError`). Likewise,
with no recorded error, a reply whose final turn ends in a failed idle marker
(even one with text) and a textless reply with no idle marker both still fail
closed as a generic `ProviderError` (`v2 session failed without recorded error
detail`) with `finish` dropped, so name-based handling such as the Lean
runner's exemption does not apply to them either. A known gap, also unchanged: the
adapter does not read an assistant entry's own `error` field.

Unchanged: a reply that ends with `finish: "stop"`, `"tool-calls"`, `"error"`
or `"unknown"` (the reader ignores those values), so an empty completed reply
is still the provider-refusal signal the Epic phase-review bash retry reads.
A truncated step earlier in the turn does not fail a turn whose last step
finished normally.

## Why

Tracked in #3165 G.8: #3175 closed this on OpenCode 1, but the v2 adapter never
carried the field. `finish` is part of the OpenCode 2 assistant entry
(`SessionMessageAssistant` in `@opencode/client` 2.0.26 through 2.2.7).

## Migration

None.

# Fix: the project DB, plugin init and the shared `.swarm` write paths refuse a blank project root

## What

A blank or whitespace project directory names no project, but several
`.swarm/` stores resolved it against `process.cwd()` and read or wrote
`.swarm/` in whatever directory the process happened to run in:

- `getProjectDb` (the shared `.swarm/swarm.db` handle) created and opened
  `<cwd>/.swarm/swarm.db`. It now throws a typed `ProjectDbError` with the new
  category `invalid_root`. `projectDbPath` throws the same error;
  `projectDbExists` returns false and `withProjectDbReadOnly` returns null for a
  blank root, so neither can report a database found under the cwd.
  `closeProjectDb` ignores a blank root instead of closing the cwd project's
  handle.
- `getDiagnoseData` (`/swarm diagnose`) diagnosed the cwd. For a blank or
  relative root it now returns one failing "Project directory" check.
- The consensus corpus read `<cwd>/.swarm/`: `listTrajectorySessions` listed
  `.swarm

# Shell write-gate walk fixpoint

## What

Six shell write-gate fixes, collated from #3586 + #3588 + #3591 (the
residuals of the #3491 → #3590 hardening series). One defect class: the
gate's static shell model admitted whenever its bounded walk stopped before
the shell semantics did.

1. **Loops whose directory state alternates no longer admit iteration-2
   writes (#3586).** `cd src; for i in 1 2; do echo x > f; cd ..; done` was
   admitted with the write judged at iteration 1's directory, while real
   bash writes `f` at the workspace root on iteration 2. When one full
   loop iteration's landing differs from the loop's ENTRY state, every
   write the loop collected — `while`/`until` clause writes included — is
   withdrawn fail-closed. The comparison basis is the PRE-clause entry
   state, so a `cd` living in the re-executing clause drifts too:
   `cd src/sub; i=0; while cd ..; [ "$i" -lt 2 ]; do i=$((i+1)); echo x >
   f; done` (real bash writes `src/f` and then the escaping
   workspace-root `f`) now denies. Net-zero loop bodies (no net `cd`)
   keep admitting. The only exemption is a `for` whose word list is a
   single fully-literal word (no glob, brace, tilde, `!` or expansion) in
   a command with no dynamic-execution builtin anywhere in the analyzed
   AST as seen after wrapper preprocessing (trap, alias, set, shopt, …;
   segment-leading `eval`/`exec`/`builtin`/`source` are unwrapped by
   preprocessing before this census and so do not contribute — the
   wrapper-collapse residual below covers what that omission means):
   that loop runs exactly once, so `cd src; for i
   in x; do echo x > f; cd ..; done` still admits.
2. **Two-level launcher chains surface their inner write targets
   (#3588).** `nice sudo time -o src/ok.txt true` lost the inner `time -o`
   target; the detector now follows launcher-headed tails to any depth
   (bounded).
3. **Nested command-less `sudo` denies (#3588).** `sudo sudo -i`,
   `sudo FOO=bar sudo -i`, `nice sudo -i` and `nice sudo -z true` were
   admitted; the launcher-uncertainty channel now re-walks nested launcher
   tails.
4. **Non-plain payload words under `sudo -i`/`-s` deny (#3588).** Any tail
   word carrying whitespace, a shell operator, a quote, `$`, or brace/comma
   structure now denies; plain multiword tails (`sudo -i make build`) keep
   admitting. One shape was a verified bypass: sudo 1.9.15p5 leaves `$`
   unescaped when it re-joins the words for the login shell's `-c`, so
   `sudo -s 'touch$IFS/tmp/x'` creates the file. The rest
   (`sudo -i 'echo x > ../esc'`, `${IFS}`, `{a,b}`) reach the shell as one
   literal word on that sudo version, so those denials are conservative:
   other sudo builds, including sudo-rs, have not been checked.
5. **`sudo -D DIR -e FILE` denies relative edit targets (#3588).**
   `cd src; sudo -D /etc -e shadow` was admitted. sudo 1.9.15p5 opens edit
   targets against the invoking directory, and `-D` only moves the
   editor's working directory, so #3588's premise that the target lands
   under DIR is wrong on that version. Other sudo builds are unverified,
   so relative targets under `-D` now deny as unresolved. Absolute targets
   are judged as written.
6. **Plain, quoted-flag, and late-flag `rm` are scope-checked (#3591).**
   Policy decision (AC10): **scope containment, modeled on
   `unlink`/`rmdir`** — every operand of a non-recursive, non-forced `rm`
   (flagless, or `-i`/`-v`) is now judged against the declared scope, so
   `rm ../esc` denies and `rm src/temp.ts` keeps admitting. GNU option
   permutation is honored — flags AFTER operands (`rm foo -rf
   ../../outside`) AND quote-spelled flags (`rm "-rf" ../../outside`,
   `rm '-f' x`) are classified by the same shared parse (bash strips the
   quotes), so quoted recursive/forced shapes hit the same guards as
   their unquoted twins: the protected-`.git`/`.swarm` arm, the
   filesystem-root guard, the traversal guard, and the build/cache
   allowli

# swarm-pr-feedback drives a PR to merge; new session-retrospective skill

`swarm-pr-feedback` used to stop once known feedback was closed. Driving CI, merging, and reviewing the session each needed a separate instruction every session. Run on a PR, the skill now carries the PR through to the end.

## Drive to merge (new `references/drive-to-merge.md`)
- **Intake.** The run takes this session's own review findings and every PR comment with findings, and runs the existing Stage A → Stage B → closeout gates.
- **Dispositions.** It plans every unfixed item's disposition before the closeout gate. It publishes them after the push is verified, or after a verified no-change outcome, and publishes any disposition added later before it checks the merge preconditions.
- **CI to green, within a budget:**
  - one rerun per infrastructure signature;
  - failures proven on the base branch become `PRE_EXISTING` dispositions, not PR fixes;
  - at most 2 fix attempts per signature and 5 fix cycles per run, counting CI-driven and review-driven rounds alike.

  Under Profile A each fix is a new controller generation.
- **Merge:**
  - **Authorization.** Only the user's own words asking for the merge in the current run authorize it, or a yes to the run's own "merge now?" question; a question, negation, hypothetical, or quoted mention of merging never does. A skill invocation, `[MODE: PR_FEEDBACK]` signal, default prompt, monitor wake, or loop activation never authorizes a merge. An injected event or PR-monitor wake also neither answers that question nor ends the wait for it.
  - **Merge command.** It uses `--match-head-commit` on the gated head. Inside the run every `gh pr`, `gh run`, and `gh repo` call and every GraphQL query is bound to the PR's resolved owner and repository (`--repo <owner>/<repo>`); swarm-ci-monitor's merge commands carry `--repo` too. It passes no strategy flag on a merge-queue base, and passes the repository's single allowed method on a direct base (or asks when several are allowed).
  - **Monitoring.** It monitors the merge queue until the merge commit is on the base. Any merge precondition that cannot become true, an unanswered question, or a monitoring ceiling ends the run with a report and the close-out steps; stopping monitoring never dequeues the PR. The final report says whether a PR monitor is still subscribed and, if the PR did not merge, asks whether to unsubscribe it.
- **Close out, merged or not:**
  1. re-verify every disposition on its live artifact;
  2. run a session retrospective;
  3. run the memory closeout.

  "Fixes only" skips CI and the merge; "don't merge" skips only the merge. Runs started by a PR-monitor wake keep their triage scope.

## Follow-up dispositions
- `references/followup-dispositions.md` now states two rules explicitly:
  - anything the PR introduced is fixed in the PR;
  - a verified, consequential defect is never closed on the agent's own judgment.
- In practice FILE means Priority items or user-approved Improvements.
- Every ASK item, follow-up proposal, Improvement, and enhancement idea goes through its own critic call before it reaches the user, and the critic's verdict travels with the question. The closeout critic gate does not count as that call.
- Priority FILE items also get a critic call before filing. A kill or downgrade makes one an ASK. If the critic is unavailable, the item is still filed, marked "not critic-reviewed" in the issue body and the ledger, and listed in the final report.
- A reviewer's severity label (`nit`, `non-blocking`) never replaces verification.

## New `session-retrospective` skill
- An evidence-based retrospective of the whole session, reconstructed from the harness's own history:
  - Claude Code transcript JSONL;
  - ZCode `~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite`, read-only;
  - Codex rollout JSONL;
  - OpenCode session store.
- It reports:
  - what worked and what failed;
  - tool and skill friction;
  - prioritized improvement

# File-authority denial messages now bounded and home-redacted

## What changed

Every `WRITE BLOCKED: Agent "…" is not authorised to write "…"` denial thrown by the shell
write gate and the file-write path now renders the target through one shared
bounded-and-redacted helper (`sanitizeDiagnosticText(redactPath(target), 320)` with the
escaping-relative home fold below), replacing raw interpolation at all four throw sites
(universal deny prefix, lenient verifier-config, enforced authority, and the non-shell
file_write door — agent names are bounded there too).

The shared `redactPath` now classifies profile shapes **lexically** on a normalized
slash form, on every host: normalization-created home paths (`/tmp/../home/<name>/…`,
`/home//<name>/…`) fold, exact profile roots (`/home/<name>`, `/Users/<name>`,
`C:\Users\<name>`) fold, and Windows-drive and UNC profile forms fold in either separator
flavor even on POSIX hosts (`C:/Users/<name>/…`, `//server/Users/<name>/…`). A folded
Windows path renders `~\rest` (the old `~\\rest` double separator is gone); non-profile paths
render exactly as before.

The file-authority denial **reason** keeps its workspace-relative display: an ESCAPING
relative path (normalized form starting `../`, provably outside the workspace) folds its
`home/<name>` / `Users/<name>` segment to `~`, and every other display routes through
`redactPath`. The denial message's target slot makes the same escaping decision on the
normalized form (`./../home/<name>/…`, `src/../../home/<name>/…`, and win32
`..\Users\<name>\…` all fold), so for operand-shaped targets — the non-shell file_write door —
the message and reason agree. The three SHELL doors render the RESOLVED absolute target: its
leading runtime profile folds, but an interior caller-supplied `home/<name>` segment beyond it
stays visible in the message while the reason folds it (folding interior segments of resolved
paths would over-redact legitimate in-workspace denial targets). Ordinary in-workspace relative
paths and non-home absolutes render structurally unchanged — through `redactPath`'s
host-normalized form, as before (over-redaction is pinned against).

Known bounds: when the workspace sits under one profile and the target under a SIBLING profile,
the relative display's common-ancestor prefix already dropped the `Users` segment, so the
sibling account name remains in the reason (the message's target slot is still folded); the
escaping fold is case-sensitive (`Users` but not `users`); a drive-relative win32 spelling
(`C:..\Users\<name>\…`, no separator after the drive) is not recognized as escaping, so the
message renders it raw while the reason folds it; and the lstat-failed / symlink-junction
ancestor denial arms still render the raw ancestor path (pre-existing, tracked for a
follow-up).

Diagnostic-only change: `ShellWriteBlockedError.writeTarget` stays exact; audit rows keep
their redacted-and-truncated contract and pick up the same profile folds (ordinary paths
persist unchanged); message shape is unchanged, so downstream message-parsing and the pinned
denial suites are unaffected.

## Why

Follow-up from PR #3568's final critic (#3587): a long attacker-influenced target (400+ chars)
flowed unbounded and un-redacted into denial messages — including absolute user-profile paths
(`C:\Users\<name>\…`) rendered verbatim. The PR #3567 round had fixed exactly one of the five
denial-throw sites; this closes the remaining four plus the reason channel.

Issue: #3587

# Fail the observability append closed at the safe-integer generation ceiling

## What

The no-bump observability append (`appendObservabilityStateWhileLocked`) now
refuses to write when the durable `observabilityRevision` generation sits at
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`: the append branch throws
`BLOCKED: PR workflow gate observability generation is exhausted at the
safe-integer ceiling; the durable row requires a manual generation reset`
instead of computing
